findings.title: Downsizing can permanently discard animation frames
findings.body: When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage` uses its non-animated conversion path, which reads only `from[0]`. Because this call uses the same path for input and output, an oversized animated GIF is replaced with a still image and its remaining frames are lost. Thumbnail settings should not silently destroy animation in the uploaded file.

findings.title: The client-side limit now ignores configured attachment sizes
findings.body: This fixed 10 MB limit is applied to both images and attachments, bypassing the configured per-type limits. For example, installations that allow attachments larger than 10 MB will have valid uploads rejected in the browser; installations with a lower attachment limit will let users submit files the server then rejects. Keep attachment validation tied to its configured limit.

findings.title: The second method definition overwrites the width/height form
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument list, so this definition replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition immediately above it. Existing callers using the previously supported width/height arguments will now pass the height as `opts` or raise an argument error, breaking those callers. Use a single method that handles both forms or update all callers.
